title: But I Love You
editorial_note: The translation keeps the refrain as faith against logic and death.

title: From the Motionless Beloved...
text:
From the motionless beloved


My God, I offer you my pain:

It is all I can offer you!

You gave me a love, one single love,

a great love!


Death stole it from me

...and nothing remains to me but my pain.

Accept it, Lord;

It is all I can now offer you!...
editorial_note: The translation preserves the offering of grief as the only remaining gift.

title: Little Sonnet
text:
Dawn in blushes

your face resembles:

do not open your eyes,

for night is falling!


Close —if anger

the light offers you—

the red lips,

for day is breaking!


Shadow in profusion,

light: you are truly mine!

Dark eyes:


very good night!

Ripe lips:

very good day!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the playful opposition of dark eyes and ripe lips.

title: To a Frenchwoman
text:
Evil, which in its resources is profuse,

never had qualms in vile parody:

Mephistopheles is an oblique Christ

who wears his mustaches twisted.


And you, who are unctuous as a prayer

and spotless and simple as a tuberose,

have tragic mane gilded by fire

and yellow pupils of leopard.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the sharp contrast between saintly surface and leopard-like danger.

title: Ejaculatory Prayer of the Snow
text:
How miraculous Nature is!

For does not snow give light? Immaculate

and mysterious, trembling and silent,

it seems to me that mutely it prays

as it falls... Oh snowfall!:

may your weightless and glacial eucharist

today absolve me of the sin of living

and make my soul, like you, become

fulgent, white, silent and cold.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the snow as a cold eucharistic absolution.

title: Offering
text:
Lord, You watered the fields with flowers

that fill the air with aroma and freshness,

you covered the heavens with immense splendors

and gave the seas their eternal murmur.


Everywhere your matchless love shines;

the earth proclaims your glory everywhere;

and amid those hymns that spring from the world,

I want to raise to you my voice of pleasure.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the hymn of fields, heavens, seas, and grateful voice.
